Table of Contents. No figure.

--- page 3 ---
Narrative text (Overview/Summary/Executive summary): framework endorsed by USG/ERC 14 Sept 2021; CERF allocated $7.5M for typhoon season 2021/2022; targets ~270,500 people (54,100 HH) with multi-purpose cash in Region 5 (Bicol) and Region 8 (Eastern Visayas). 2-stage trigger: (1) Readiness trigger 4-7 days pre-landfall — TC category ≥4 (>200 km/h max 1-min sustained wind), projected to hit Region 5/8; (2) Activation trigger on/before 72hrs (3 days) pre-landfall — 510 model impact estimate meets threshold: 50% probability ≥80,000 houses totally damaged to 95% probability ≥5,000 houses totally damaged.

--- page 4 ---
Narrative text (The Delivery): no figure. Key numbers: 66% of CERF AA pilot budget via cash (multi-purpose + sectoral top-ups); $58 (75% of avg regional wage for 10 days + transport) blanket cash to 54,100 HH/270,500 beneficiaries by WFP, FAO, IOM; FAO targets 16,000 agri-households + 80,000 agri-households for advisories; safe-storage for 500 HH; PRC cash-for-work to 150 HH; Oxfam cash for 50 families; IOM CCCM kits to 13,110 families, shelter kits to 11,970 families; UNFPA protection commodities to 5,000 women/girls, cash-for-work to 810 volunteers, cash vouchers to 3,000 pregnant women, GoBags to 7,000 adolescent girls; UNICEF sectoral top-ups (nutrition, education, child protection, WASH) reaching safe water for 10,000 vulnerable HH.

Narrative text (Introduction/Objectives) plus a diagram "What does collective anticipatory action look like?" showing pipeline: Robust Forecasting & Decision-making Framework → Established Action Plans → Pre-arranged Financing → Anticipatory Action → Reduced Crisis. Objective: reach ~270,500 people with multi-purpose cash ahead of typhoon landfall in Region 5 & 8.

--- page 7 ---
Narrative text (Core principles list of 9; Tropical Cyclones in the Philippines stats): Philippines ranked 3rd for disaster risk (World Risk Report 2018, index 25%); 60% of land area exposed to multiple hazards, 74% of population susceptible (GFDRR 2017); ~20 tropical cyclones enter PAR/year, ~5 destructive; TCs with wind ≥118-220 km/h cause significant impact; active season June-Nov, least active May.

(2) "PHILIPPINES Humanitarian Country Team Minimum Operations Protocol for Tropical Cyclone" (as of 20 May 2021) — a 5-stage timeline infographic (Preparedness → Readiness [landfall minus 6 days] → Activation [landfall minus 3 days] → Response [landfall plus 1-5 days] → Monitoring [landfall +1wk to 3mos]) with detailed actions per stage.

Narrative on known challenges: 150km track-position error 72h ahead for Typhoon Goni; past storms tested against trigger (Haiyan 2013, Hagupit 2014, Nock-ten 2016, Kammuri 2019, Goni 2020) — only 3 (Haiyan, Nock-ten, Kammuri) would reach activation trigger.

--- page 15 ---
Narrative text, no figure (Operational coordination with local authorities; Mandatory pre-emptive evacuation procedure). Key facts: post-Haiyan (6,000+ casualties) evacuation procedures; evacuations begin 48h before landfall, complete 24h before; return 12h after landfall; COVID-19 pushes prep start to 72h before landfall.

--- page 34 ---
Annex 3 — Evaluation of forecasts (April 2021): narrative on selecting IFRC/DREF model over Global Parametrics and WFP models (operational track record, open-source, admin-3 resolution, PAGASA integration). Table: "Evaluation Matrix" comparing IFRC/DREF, Global Parametrics, WFP on criterion "trigger based on public forecast data" and "uses PAGASA data" (IFRC/DREF: ECMWF-based, not yet PAGASA; Global Parametrics: multi-agency forecasts incl. PAGASA; WFP: CHIRPS/ERA5 + PAGASA precip, not public) and "trigger simplicity" (IFRC/DREF partial - ML model; Global Parametrics partial - windspeed probability threshold; WFP yes - simple rainfall anomaly threshold).

--- page 35 ---
Table continuation of Evaluation Matrix: lead time (IFRC/DREF & Global Parametrics: yes, 72h+; WFP: N/A, doesn't use forecast data), adaptability by June (IFRC/DREF: yes; Global Parametrics: partial; WFP: likely not), open source (IFRC/DREF: yes; others: no/could be), cost to operationalize (IFRC/DREF: low; Global Parametrics: medium; WFP: unclear), model performance (IFRC/DREF: precision/recall ~70%; Global Parametrics: accurately called major storms since 2019; WFP: 17% precision for Bicol). Below: "Model Card - IFRC/DREF" begins (contacts, model link, intended use: map of predicted % completely damaged buildings per municipality, all Philippines at admin level 3).

--- page 36 ---
Narrative text (IFRC/DREF model card continued: hazard data=ECMWF TC/wind forecasts; vulnerability=NDRRMC housing damage reports; methodology=Willoughby wind-field method + XGBoost; threshold=10% houses totally damaged in ≥3 municipalities, 1-in-5-year; classification+regression models; performance precision/recall/F1 ~0.7, MAE 3%/RMSE 7%; used since 2019 incl. Tisoy 2019, Ulysses 2020, missed Goni 2020). Figure: "TYPHOON TRIGGER MODEL: Technical Overview" (510 Red Cross) — a 6-step flow diagram showing explanatory variables (exposure/vulnerability indicators: roof type, poverty, wall type; hazard indicators: rainfall, wind speed, typhoon path, sustained duration) combined via historical typhoon data (Haiyan, Melor, Hagupit, Nammasun) to build a model predicting # damaged houses by municipality, applied to current typhoon (Haima) with a small Philippines damage map thumbnail.

--- page 37 ---
"Model Card - Global Parametrics": contacts, model link, intended use (output = probability of exceeding a specific wind speed at a location; scope = Salcedo, Eastern Samar, expanding). Hazard data from NASA/UKMET/NOAA/CPHC/JTWC/etc + PAGASA; vulnerability = Oxfam socioeconomic/housing data; methodology = typhoon track wind fields per ensemble member, fraction above threshold if ≥5 tracks; validated since 2019; ready to deploy pending new geographies; tested against 2019/2020 TCs (3 key events captured) by Oxfam.

--- page 38 ---
Figure: "Methodology" slide (Global Parametrics) showing 3 maps for TC Phanfone (22-12-19): (1) wind speed color scale 5-50 m/s overlay near Philippines; (2) historical ensemble track map (pink/green lines) over Philippines/Vietnam/South China Sea; (3) zoomed wind-speed heatmap over central Philippines with small highlighted (green) area = Salcedo, Eastern Samar. Below: "Model Card - WFP" begins: output = anomalous rainfall % + trigger threshold; scope = full national, admin level 2; hazard data = NOAA IBTracks + CHIRPS/PAGASA precipitation anomalies; vulnerability = ReliefWeb affected-people data.

--- page 39 ---
Narrative text (WFP model card continued): methodology = binary classification (affected/not affected), vulnerability+socioeconomic index combined with hazard for risk index; threshold via ROC curve on precipitation anomaly; performance = 17% precision for Region V (Bicol) at 28% rainfall anomaly threshold; not yet used operationally for AA (needs switch from real-time to forecast data). Chart: "HAZARD TIMELINE – Region V" — dual-panel time series 2010-2021: top panel shows rainfall "Anomalies (%) - Mean" fluctuating roughly -50% to +150% over time; bottom panel (log scale) shows "Affected People" (10^3 to 10^7) as dots colored by hazard type (Flood=blue, Tropical storms/typhoons=red, Dry spell=orange), with vertical lines linking anomaly spikes to affected-people events across the 2010-2021 period.
